If your meat has blood in it, then something is seriously wrong. The watery red juice from red meat is myoglobin. Myoglobin is an iron- and oxygen-binding protein found in the muscle tissue of vertebrates in general and in almost all mammals. It is distantly related to hemoglobin which is the iron- and oxygen-binding protein in blood, specifically in the red blood cells. In humans, myoglobin is only found in the bloodstream after muscle injury. It is an abnormal finding, and can be diagnostically relevant when found in blood. Animal muscle tissue should have no blood in it unless there was an injury that introduced blood into a localized area of the tissue. You don't want blood in your hamburger, even if you paid for it.
